text:
The massive, 50-foot swells along California’s coast this weekend foretold an intense week of towering waves to come.
Officials from the National Weather Service (NWS) had issued advisories for long stretches of the California coast, warning people that erratic and unpredictable waves could quickly overpower anyone nearby. The highest waves – which reached 50 to 60ft (15.24 to 18.29 meters) – cracked along the popular Mavericks surf spot in San Mateo county, south of San Francisco.
In the coming days, officials said weather models are predicting more storms, this time coming from a more westerly direction that could expose slightly different parts of the coast to monster waves – which could peak around 20ft (6.1 meters).
High surf and coastal flood advisories were in effect throughout the weekend, and about 270 homes in Santa Cruz county were under evacuation warnings.
Even more rain and high surf are expected to follow. “It’s going to be a busy couple of weeks – be ready,” said Brian Garcia, a meteorologist from the NWS.
The low-pressure system that brought rain across the Bay Area on Sunday will be followed by large waves on Monday night. Tornado warnings were in effect for parts of Santa Cruz county through Monday afternoon.
Midweek, a powerful storm building along the Pacific is expected to bring between 1.5 and 6in (3.81 to 15.24cm) of rain across the Bay Area as well as fierce winds of up to 50 miles per hour (80.46 km/h).
Huge waves usually accompany a strong El Niño – and this year’s is predicted to be the strongest ever recorded, with global implications. El Niños are a naturally recurring phenomenon where the eastern Pacific temporarily heats up, causing global changes in weather patterns. Some research suggests that global heating is making El Ninõs more powerful. Scientists have also warned that the current, record-setting El Niño will be a “risk multiplier” – warping global weather patterns that have fueled wildfires and crop failures in Indonesia, coastal inundation in the US, severe drought in Sudan, and severe flooding in several countries.
In California, officials are expecting coastal wells, but also more intense storms and erratic weather through the next several months.
This week, the two Pacific storms are expected to impact not only the coast but huge swathes of the eastern US, bringing gusty winds, rain and heavy mountain snow in the Sierra Nevadas, according to NWS.
digest_he: תושבי קליפורניה נערכים לגל נוסף של סערות עוצמתיות וגלים בגובה של עשרות רגלים הצפויים לפקוד את חופי המדינה. שירות מזג האוויר הלאומי פרסם אזהרות חמורות והנחיות פינוי למאות בתים במחוז סנטה קרוז, תוך הדגשה כי תנאי מזג האוויר הבלתי צפויים עלולים לסכן חיי אדם. גלים עצומים בגובה של עד שישים רגל נשברו באזור הגלישה הפופולרי סן מטאו, והרשויות מדווחים כי מערכת חורפית משמעותית צפויה להביא עמה משבי רוח חזקים, כמויות משקעים משמעותיות וסיכון לשיטפונות. תופעות קיצוניות אלו מקושרות בין היתר לתופעת אל ני뇨 חזקה במיוחד המשפיעה על דפוסי מזג האוויר הגלובליים, וגורמי החירום קוראים לציבור לנקוט משנה זהירות לקראת הימים הקרובים.
